title: A dad built his first game in 20 years with Grok in about 5 hours. Here's what he said about it
author: shaymagen
selftext:
Hi all, I run Vibe1Up, a small free site that lists browser games made with AI. I wanted to share our first ever community submission because his story made my week.

The game is BRITBOX by Simon Ball. It's a silly British meme game built on a wojak template. Here's what he told me:

"This is the first game I've released since I was a teenager about 20 odd years ago"

"I have a young family and work full time, so my available time is minimal, so being able to develop while I'm running around has been invaluable, otherwise I just wouldn't have done anything."

"I got this operational in about 5 hours. I saw the meme template in my lunchbreak, had the idea and then published it the morning after."

He said the hardest part was the art: "ensuring that the right likeness transferred over to the game was the bit with the most back and forth."

You can play it here (it runs in the browser, free, no sign-up): https://vibe1up.com/game/britbox/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=social&utm\_campaign=aigamedev

For those of you who use AI on art, how do you keep a character's likeness consistent across sprites?
